docs.title: Luau API reference
docs.text: Generated by Apogee.Runtime --luau-docs from the engine's registry: do not edit. The same information, as type definitions for luau-lsp, is apogee.d.luau (--luau-defs).

docs.title: Globals
docs.text:
What the host sets in the VMs it runs scripts in.

  • world: World. The world the script runs in (--run sets it).
  • physics: PhysicsWorld. The physics of the world: give entities bodies with physics:add_body, ask what is where with physics:raycast. It is stepped before the world each frame.
  • audio: AudioSystem. The game's sound: audio:load_sound and the sounds it plays need OpenAL Soft installed (audio.is_active says); an entity with the AudioListener component is the ear.
  • steam: SteamSystem. The game's connection to Steam (the base game only; mods cannot use it): achievements, stats, leaderboards, rich presence, the overlay, cloud saves and Workshop mods. steam.is_active says whether Steam is running; when it is not every call does nothing.
  • net: NetSystem. The game's network (the base game only; mods cannot use it): net:listen(port) and net:connect(address) make NetConnections, connection:send(text) sends, and the signals connection_requested, connected, message and disconnected say what happened. net.is_active says whether the network library is installed; when it is not every call does nothing.
  • models: ModelLibrary. The models entities draw: models:load(path) returns the id to put in a ModelRenderer component (the same id for the same path, 0 means none). A game with an entity that has the MainCamera component is drawn through it; Light entities light it.
  • ui: UiSystem. The game's user interface: ui:load_document(path) loads RML from a file, ui:create_document() makes an empty one; documents can carry <script>s, on* attributes and data models (ui:open_data_model); elements are UiElements you make, move and listen to. It is sized to the screen, fed the player's input, and drawn over the picture.
  • input: InputActionRouter. The player's input as actions: define them on input.map, set input.contexts each frame, read input:get_strength(action) and connect input.action_fired.

docs.title: Classes
docs.text:
• AudioBus: A bus of the mix: a group of sounds with a volume, a mute and a pause of its own (Music, Vehicles, Environment, UI).
  • AudioSound: A sound file loaded by AudioSystem.LoadSound: play it any number of times, on any bus.
  • AudioSystem: The game's audio, on OpenAL Soft: sounds (WAV, FLAC, MP3, Ogg Vorbis) played in 3D around the entity that has an AudioListener, on buses, with reverb zones and occlusion.
  • AudioVoice: Something that is playing, or about to: a sound on a source (AudioSound.Play).
  • BodyDesc: What a body is made of and how it behaves: the shape, how it moves, its mass, surface and layers.
  • CharacterController: A walking character: a capsule that slides along walls, climbs stairs and slopes, sticks to the ground going down and stands on moving platforms, without being a rigid body (Jolt's CharacterVirtual).
  • Hitch: A hitch on a vehicle: a point on its body where an attachment or a trailer is attached.
  • InputActionMap: Every action the player can bind, where each works (its contexts) and what it is bound to.
  • InputActionRouter: Turns the player's input into the actions of an InputActionMap that fire in the active contexts, and says how far analog actions are pushed.
  • ModelLibrary: The models that entities draw (ModelRenderer.Model is an id from here; scripts see this as models).
  • NetConnection: One connection to another program, made by NetSystem.Connect or accepted by a NetSystem.Listen.
  • NetSystem: The game's network: connections to other programs over UDP, with encryption, in order and reliably or not as each message asks (GameNetworkingSockets, Valve's open-source transport).
  • PhysicsShape: A collision shape: an immutable thing a body (or another shape) is made of, in the body's local space.
  • PhysicsWorld: The physics simulation of one ECS World: Jolt Physics with double-precision positions, stepped at a fixed rate.
  • SteamSystem
  • UiDataModel: A data model: a script's table tied to documents.
  • UiElement: An element of a document (a div, a text node, a whole document) as scripts hold it.
  • UiEvent: An event that reached a listener (UiElement.Listen).
  • UiSystem
  • Vehicle: A vehicle on a dynamic body: wheels with suspension and tires, or tracks, an engine and a clutch (Jolt's VehicleConstraint).
  • VehicleDesc: A vehicle: its engine, drivetrain and wheels.
  • WheelDesc: One wheel of a vehicle.
  • World

docs.title: Libraries
docs.text:
• debug_draw: Debug drawing for Luau scripts, as the global table debug_draw: lines and shapes that last one frame, drawn over the world.
  • defs
  • devtools: The devtools table of scripts: when to draw, and what to show in the debug window.
  • fs
  • game: What a game asks of the program that runs it, as the script table game: ending the run (a menu's Quit), and whether the Escape key still ends it.
  • imgui: Dear ImGui for Luau scripts, as the global table imgui: snake_case functions over the same calls the dev tools use.
  • packages
  • xml

docs.title: AudioBus
docs.text:
Extends EngineObject.

A bus of the mix: a group of sounds with a volume, a mute and a pause of its own (Music, Vehicles, Environment, UI). See AudioSystem.GetBus.

docs.title: Properties
docs.text:
• name: string Read-only.
  • volume: number The volume, 0 to 1 and above. The volume of the master bus is AudioSystem.Volume.
  • muted: boolean

docs.title: set_paused
docs.text:
function set_paused(self, paused: boolean): ()

Pauses everything on the bus, and resumes it.

docs.title: AudioSound
docs.text:
Extends EngineObject.

A sound file loaded by AudioSystem.LoadSound: play it any number of times, on any bus.

docs.title: Properties
docs.text:
• path: string Read-only.
  • is3_d: boolean Read-only.
  • min_distance: number The distance in meters up to which the sound is not made quieter (inverse-distance rolloff starts here): 1. Voices of this sound start with it.
  • max_distance: number The distance in meters beyond which the sound gets no quieter: 10000. Voices of this sound start with it.
  • length: number The length in seconds (0 when the file does not say). Read-only.

docs.title: play
docs.text:
function play(self, bus: string?, volume: number?, pitch: number?, loop: boolean?, entity: Entity?): AudioVoice

Plays it on bus (see AudioSystem.GetBus; empty is the master mix), at this volume and pitch, looping if asked (or if it was loaded with loop), following entity if given. Returns the voice.

docs.title: AudioSystem
docs.text:
Extends EngineObject.

The game's audio, on OpenAL Soft: sounds (WAV, FLAC, MP3, Ogg Vorbis) played in 3D around the entity that has an AudioListener, on buses, with reverb zones and occlusion. OpenAL Soft is a separate shared library that ships beside the program (see Legal/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md): without it IsActive is false, every call does nothing and returns something inert, and the game runs in silence.

docs.title: Properties
docs.text:
• is_active: boolean True when OpenAL started: sounds will play. False means every call is a no-op. Read-only.
  • physics: PhysicsWorld? The physics world that casts the rays for AudioVoice.Occlusion.
  • volume: number The master volume, 0 to 1 and above.
  • current_reverb: ReverbPreset The reverb the listener hears now: the preset of the zone it is in, or ReverbPreset.Off. Read-only.

docs.title: update
docs.text:
function update(self, deltaSeconds: number): ()

Once a frame, after the world has progressed: finds the listeners, puts the voices where their entities are (relative to the nearest listener, in double precision, with the velocities the Doppler effect needs), raycasts the occlusion, picks the reverb zone, and mixes the time that has passed when the output is not a device. deltaSeconds is the game's frame time.

docs.title: get_bus
docs.text:
function get_bus(self, name: string): AudioBus

A bus by name, made when first asked for: the groups of sounds a game mixes (music, vehicles, ui), each with a volume, a mute and a pause of its own. The empty name and master are the whole mix (its volume is Volume). Buses are cached: asking twice gives the same object.

docs.title: load_sound
docs.text:
function load_sound(self, path: string, stream: boolean?, is3D: boolean?, loop: boolean?): AudioSound

Loads a sound file (WAV, FLAC, MP3 or Ogg Vorbis) from the file system. stream decodes it as it plays instead of whole (music, long ambience); is3D makes it positional; loop loops it by default.

docs.title: create
docs.text:
AudioSystem.create: (ecs: World) -> AudioSystem

Makes an audio system for an ECS world from a script, mixing into nowhere (no sound device is opened): for tests. A game's own is the global audio.

docs.title: is_installed
docs.text:
AudioSystem.is_installed: () -> boolean

Whether OpenAL Soft and the decoders can be loaded: false on a machine without the libraries.

docs.title: AudioVoice
docs.text:
Extends EngineObject.

Something that is playing, or about to: a sound on a source (AudioSound.Play). Attach it to an entity to make it positional: it then follows that entity's world transform, with the velocity for Doppler, and is set relative to the nearest listener in double precision. A voice from an inactive audio system (no OpenAL) is inert: it never plays.

docs.title: Properties
docs.text:
• entity: Entity The entity the voice follows in 3D, or 0 for a voice that is not positional (or sits at the listener).
  • occlusion: boolean Check the way from the listener with the physics world's rays and muffle the sound behind walls (smoothly): needs AudioSystem.Physics and an Entity.
  • volume: number
  • pitch: number Playback speed and pitch together: 1 is as recorded, 2 an octave up.
  • min_distance: number The distance in meters up to which the voice is not made quieter.
  • max_distance: number The distance in meters beyond which the voice gets no quieter.
  • paused: boolean
  • is_playing: boolean Whether it is still sounding (a paused sound is). Read-only.
  • position: number The playback position in seconds. Read-only.
  • muffling: number How much the sound is muffled by what is between it and the listener, 0 (nothing) to 1. Read-only.

docs.title: BodyDesc
docs.text:
Extends EngineObject.

What a body is made of and how it behaves: the shape, how it moves, its mass, surface and layers. Fill one in and give it to PhysicsWorld.AddBody; the same description can make any number of bodies. Where the body is comes from its entity's transform (its scale is applied to the shape).

Create one with BodyDesc.new().

docs.title: Properties
docs.text:
• shape: PhysicsShape? What it collides as. Required.
  • motion: MotionKind
  • mass: number The mass in kilograms of a dynamic body; 0 takes it from the shape's volume and Density.
  • density: number Kilograms per cubic meter, for a body with no Mass (water is 1000).
  • friction: number
  • restitution: number How much of its speed a body keeps when it bounces: 0 to 1.
  • linear_damping: number The fraction of linear speed lost per second.
  • angular_damping: number
  • gravity_factor: number 1 is the world's gravity, 0 none, negative lifts.
  • layers: number The collision layers the body is in, a bit each (PhysicsLayers).
  • mask: number The layers it collides with.
  • is_sensor: boolean A sensor does not collide: it reports the bodies inside it (PhysicsWorld.SensorEntered).
  • events: boolean Report its contacts (PhysicsWorld.ContactBegan) and when it wakes or sleeps. Off by default: events cost something for every pair.
  • allow_sleeping: boolean
  • bullet: boolean Check the whole path of a fast body instead of its position at each step (bullets, fast wheels), so it cannot tunnel through thin walls. Costs more.
  • center_of_mass: Vector3? Where the center of mass is, in the body's space, when it is not where the shape's volume puts it (a truck's engine and axles are low: (0, 0.9, 0.5)). Unset keeps the shape's. A vehicle drives well only with a low center.
  • linear_velocity: Vector3
  • angular_velocity: Vector3

docs.title: CharacterController
docs.text:
Extends EngineObject.

A walking character: a capsule that slides along walls, climbs stairs and slopes, sticks to the ground going down and stands on moving platforms, without being a rigid body (Jolt's CharacterVirtual). Make one with PhysicsWorld.CreateCharacter; it moves in every fixed step toward DesiredVelocity, and its entity's transform (the feet) follows, blended between steps like a dynamic body's. Dynamic bodies are pushed by it and do not push it.

docs.title: Properties
docs.text:
• entity: Entity The entity that follows the character. Read-only.
  • desired_velocity: Vector3 The velocity the character tries to have, in meters per second, in world space. Only the horizontal part matters: gravity and jumps decide the vertical one.
  • is_on_ground: boolean Whether the character stands on something that holds it (not a slope too steep to stand on). Read-only.
  • ground_velocity: Vector3 The velocity of the ground under the character (a moving platform), or zero in the air. Read-only.
  • velocity: Vector3 How fast the character actually moved in the last step. Read-only.
  • max_slope_degrees: number The steepest slope in degrees the character can stand and walk on. Read-only.
  • position: Vector3 Where the feet are, after the last step. Read-only.

docs.title: jump
docs.text:
function jump(self, speed: number): ()

Starts a jump of this upward speed (m/s) at the next step, if the character is on the ground then.

docs.title: teleport
docs.text:
function teleport(self, position: Vector3): ()

Puts the character (its feet) here at once; its entity follows with no blend.

docs.title: set_rotation
docs.text:
function set_rotation(self, rotation: Quat): ()

Turns the character about its up axis (its entity follows).

docs.title: Hitch
docs.text:
Extends EngineObject.

A hitch on a vehicle: a point on its body where an attachment or a trailer is attached. The hitch is an entity under the vehicle's, whose transform is the hitch's frame in the vehicle's space; Attach takes the attachment's entity and the attach point in the attachment's space, which meets the hitch's frame. Make one with PhysicsWorld.CreateHitch. A hitch holds one body at a time; the pair do not collide while hitched.

docs.title: Properties
docs.text:
• hitch_entity: Entity The entity that is the hitch's frame, under the vehicle's entity. Read-only.
  • kind: HitchKind Read-only.
  • attached: Entity What is attached, or 0. Read-only.
  • is_attached: boolean Read-only.
  • angular_limits: Vector3 A trailer hitch's swing limits about the hitch's X, Y and Z, in degrees (default 25, 75, 15: pitch, yaw, roll).
  • attach_position: Vector3 Where the attachment's attach point is, in the attachment's space. Read-only.

docs.title: attach
docs.text:
function attach(self, attachment: Entity, point: Vector3, pointRotation: Quat): boolean

Attaches the body of attachment so that its point point (turned by pointRotation), in the attachment's own space, meets the hitch. False if the hitch holds something already. A mounted attachment must be a dynamic or kinematic body without a vehicle; a trailer may be a vehicle.

docs.title: detach
docs.text:
function detach(self): ()

Lets the attachment go. A mounted one gets a body of its own again where it is (it keeps moving as the point of the vehicle it was at, and its mass leaves the vehicle); a trailer's joint goes. A mounted entity is put back under the hitch's parent... in the world, in its place: it is a root again.

docs.title: InputActionMap
docs.text:
Extends EngineObject.

Every action the player can bind, where each works (its contexts) and what it is bound to. Contexts are names the game chooses (world, on_foot, vehicle, menu); situations say which are active together, so two actions that can never be active at once may share an input. A InputActionRouter turns the player's input into these actions.

Create one with InputActionMap.new().

docs.title: add_situation
docs.text:
function add_situation(self, contexts: { string }): ()

Says that these contexts are active together (a situation). Without any, two actions clash when they share a context.

docs.title: add_action
docs.text:
function add_action(self, id: string, contexts: { string }, defaults: { string }, analog: boolean?, help: string?): ()

Adds an action, bound to defaults (binding texts: see Binding). An analog action is read by strength; the others fire.

docs.title: get_actions
docs.text:
function get_actions(self): { string }

The ids of the actions, in the order they were added.

docs.title: get_help
docs.text:
function get_help(self, id: string): string

What an action is for, as it was added.

docs.title: contexts_overlap
docs.text:
function contexts_overlap(self, a: { string }, b: { string }): boolean

True when an action of a and one of b can be active at the same time.

docs.title: set_bindings
docs.text:
function set_bindings(self, id: string, bindings: { string }): ()

Rebinds an action. Throws (a script error) on a binding that does not read.

docs.title: get_conflicts
docs.text:
function get_conflicts(self, id: string, binding: string): { string }

The actions that would clash if id were bound to this text.

docs.title: get_all_conflicts
docs.text:
function get_all_conflicts(self): { string }

Every clash as a line of three tab-separated fields: the action, the other action and the binding.

docs.title: save_text
docs.text:
function save_text(self): string

Save as text, one line per action: lights = Hold L | Joy RB (an action with no binding has nothing after the equals sign).

docs.title: load_text
docs.text:
function load_text(self, text: string): { string }

Applies SaveText's text; returns what could not be applied, as Load does.

docs.title: normalize_binding
docs.text:
InputActionMap.normalize_binding: (text: string) -> string

The binding text as it would be saved: the trigger, the modifiers and the input spelled the way this class writes them. Throws (a script error) on text that does not read.

docs.title: binding_error
docs.text:
InputActionMap.binding_error: (text: string) -> string

Why a binding text does not read, or an empty string when it does.

docs.title: parse_binding
docs.text:
InputActionMap.parse_binding: (text: string) -> (string, { Modifiers }, Trigger)

A binding's parts: the input, its modifiers, its trigger. Throws (a script error) on text that does not read.

docs.title: InputActionRouter
docs.text:
Extends EngineObject.

Turns the player's input into the actions of an InputActionMap that fire in the active contexts, and says how far analog actions are pushed. Of the bindings on an input whose modifiers are all held, the one with the most modifiers wins, so Shift+Tab isn't also Tab, and a key still fires while running with Shift. A key with a hold binding fires its press on a quick release instead; a key with a double tap waits a moment for the second tap before firing its press. InputDevices feeds it from SDL; Press, Release, Axis and Poll feed it by hand, with explicit times (seconds, any origin), for tests and replays. Call Update once a frame to raise ActionFired, and EndFrame after the frame's logic ran.

Create one with InputActionRouter.new().

docs.title: Properties
docs.text:
• map: InputActionMap? The actions to route. The router takes the map over: it lives as long as the router does.
  • contexts: { string } The active contexts (a situation); none ignores every input. A game sets them every frame from what the player is doing.
  • is_gamepad_last: boolean True when the last input pressed was on a gamepad (the labels then name its buttons). Read-only.

docs.title: Signals
docs.text:
• action_fired: Signal<string>
  • captured: Signal<string> The binding text of what was pressed while Listen was on.

docs.title: listen
docs.text:
function listen(self): ()

Rebinding: the next key (with the modifiers held), mouse button, wheel step, gamepad button or stick or trigger pushed past half way is not routed; Captured gets its binding text (Shift+F, Joy LY-) at the next Update, and listening ends. A modifier key alone does not count: it waits for the key it goes with.

docs.title: press
docs.text:
function press(self, input: string, modifiers: { Modifiers }, time: number): ()

An input goes down. modifiers are the Ctrl, Shift and Alt held with it, not counting the input itself.

docs.title: release
docs.text:
function release(self, input: string, time: number): ()

An input goes up.

docs.title: axis
docs.text:
function axis(self, axis: string, value: number, time: number): ()

An axis moves: Joy LX, Joy LY, Joy RX, Joy RY (-1..1), Joy LT, Joy RT (0..1), or the mouse's motion in pixels since the last event (Mouse X, Mouse Y), which adds up until EndFrame.

docs.title: end_frame
docs.text:
function end_frame(self): ()

The frame's logic has read the mouse's motion: it starts again from zero.

docs.title: release_all
docs.text:
function release_all(self): ()

Everything let go and forgotten: the window lost focus, or the game is changing screens.

docs.title: poll
docs.text:
function poll(self, time: number): { string }

Fires what time has made due (a hold that has been held long enough, a tap that no second tap followed) and returns the actions fired since the last call, in order. An action bound to several inputs fires once for each.

docs.title: update
docs.text:
function update(self, time: number): ()

Poll, and raises ActionFired for each action and Captured for a binding that was listened for. Once a frame, before the logic that reads the actions.

docs.title: get_down
docs.text:
function get_down(self): { string }

The inputs that are down, sorted.

docs.title: get_strength
docs.text:
function get_strength(self, action: string): number

How far an action is pushed: 0 to 1 for keys, buttons, sticks and triggers (the largest of its bindings), more for the mouse's motion; 0 outside its contexts.

docs.title: get_label
docs.text:
function get_label(self, action: string): string

What to press for an action, as the player's keyboard names it (Z on AZERTY for a W binding), or its gamepad button when the gamepad was used last; an en dash when it is unbound.

docs.title: label_binding
docs.text:
InputActionRouter.label_binding: (text: string) -> string

A binding as the player reads it: Hold Ctrl+Left mouse, Pad A, and a key by what it types on their keyboard layout.

docs.title: ModelLibrary
docs.text:
Extends EngineObject.

The models that entities draw (ModelRenderer.Model is an id from here; scripts see this as models). A model is loaded once per path whatever the number of entities that show it, and reloaded in place when its file changes, so entities keep their id. Ids are never reused.

docs.title: load
docs.text:
function load(self, path: string): number

The id of the model at path, which is the same for every call with that path. The file has to exist; whether it is a model shows when it is first drawn.

docs.title: NetConnection
docs.text:
Extends EngineObject.

One connection to another program, made by NetSystem.Connect or accepted by a NetSystem.Listen. Messages are sent on it and arrive as signals of the NetSystem.

Objects of this class are refused to mods.

docs.title: Properties
docs.text:
• address: string The other side's address (the one that was asked for, for a connection we made). Read-only.
  • is_incoming: boolean True for a connection that somebody made to our port, false for one we made. Read-only.
  • state: NetState Read-only.
  • ping: number The round trip time in milliseconds, or -1 when it is not known yet. Read-only.
  • quality: number 0 to 1: the share of our packets that arrive, as the other side measures it. Read-only.
  • bytes_out: number Bytes a second being sent. Read-only.
  • bytes_in: number Bytes a second being received. Read-only.

docs.title: send
docs.text:
function send(self, data: string, reliable: boolean?, lane: number?): boolean

Sends text (UTF-8) to the other side. reliable messages arrive, once and in order; the others may be lost, never twice, and are for what is out of date a moment later (positions). lane is the lane set by ConfigureLanes (0 is the default one). Returns false when it could not be queued.

docs.title: configure_lanes
docs.text:
function configure_lanes(self, count: number): boolean

Gives the connection count lanes: messages on one lane arrive in order and a slow one does not hold up the others. Before the first message.

docs.title: close
docs.text:
function close(self, reason: string?, linger: boolean?): ()

Ends the connection. Messages still waiting are sent first when linger. The other side gets NetSystem.Disconnected with reason; here no signal is emitted (we asked for it).

docs.title: refuse
docs.text:
function refuse(self): ()

In a handler of NetSystem.ConnectionRequested: turns the connection down.

docs.title: NetSystem
docs.text:
Extends EngineObject.

The game's network: connections to other programs over UDP, with encryption, in order and reliably or not as each message asks (GameNetworkingSockets, Valve's open-source transport). One side Listens, the others Connect; messages are sent on a NetConnection. There is no replication here: what is sent, and what it means, is the game's. Without the library, IsActive is false and every call does nothing, so a game that can also play alone works the same.

Objects of this class are refused to mods.

docs.title: Properties
docs.text:
• is_active: boolean True when the library started: connections can be made. False means every call does nothing. Read-only.
  • status: string Why the system is not active, or "Ready.". Read-only.
  • listening_port: number The port being listened on (the one asked for, or the free one the library chose), or 0. Read-only.

docs.title: Signals
docs.text:
• connection_requested: Signal<NetConnection, string> Somebody wants to connect to the port we listen on, with their address. The connection is accepted when the handlers return, unless one of them called NetConnection.Refuse. Messages cannot be sent on it yet: wait for Connected.
  • connected: Signal<NetConnection> A connection is up: the one that Connect started was accepted, or a requested one is made. Messages can be sent now.
  • disconnected: Signal<NetConnection, string, number> A connection ended: the other side closed it, it timed out, or a connection that was being made failed. With the reason's text and code (1000 and up: the other side's own).
  • message: Signal<NetConnection, string, number> A message arrived on a connection, as text, on a lane.

docs.title: listen
docs.text:
function listen(self, port: number?): number

Listens on a UDP port, for IPv4 and IPv6 (0: any free port). Returns the port, or 0 if it could not be opened (it is in use, or the system is inactive). One port at a time: listening again closes the first (its connections stay).

docs.title: stop_listening
docs.text:
function stop_listening(self): ()

Stops accepting new connections; the ones made stay.

docs.title: connect
docs.text:
function connect(self, address: string): NetConnection?

Starts connecting to host:port (an IP address, [::1]:27020 for IPv6, or a name, which is looked up first and so can block for a moment). The result is a Connected or a Disconnected signal. Returns null when the address cannot be used.

docs.title: update
docs.text:
function update(self): ()

Once a frame: runs the library's callbacks and emits what happened as signals, in order: connections made, messages, connections ended.

docs.title: create
docs.text:
NetSystem.create: () -> NetSystem

Makes a network system of its own from a script: for tests, which talk to themselves over the loopback interface. A game's own is the global net.

docs.title: create_inactive
docs.text:
NetSystem.create_inactive: () -> NetSystem

Makes an inactive network system from a script: for tests of what scripts see when there is no library.

docs.title: is_installed
docs.text:
NetSystem.is_installed: () -> boolean

Whether the library can be loaded: false on a machine without GameNetworkingSockets next to the program.

docs.title: PhysicsShape
docs.text:
Extends EngineObject.

A collision shape: an immutable thing a body (or another shape) is made of, in the body's local space. Made with the static functions, given to BodyDesc.Shape, and shared freely: many bodies can use one. Jolt counts references, so a shape that a script lets go of lives on in the bodies that use it.

docs.title: Properties
docs.text:
• kind: string What it is: box, sphere, capsule, cylinder, convex_hull, mesh, height_field, compound, offset or scaled. Read-only.
  • volume: number The volume in cubic meters, which with the density gives a dynamic body its mass. Read-only.
  • center_of_mass: Vector3 The shape's center of mass, in its local space. Read-only.

docs.title: is_valid_scale
docs.text:
function is_valid_scale(self, scale: Vector3): boolean

Whether the shape can be scaled by this much (a sphere only evenly, a mesh by anything).

docs.title: box
docs.text:
PhysicsShape.box: (halfExtents: Vector3, convexRadius: number?) -> PhysicsShape

A box of these half extents, centered on the origin. The edges are rounded by convexRadius (Jolt's default, 5 cm, is shrunk for small boxes).

docs.title: capsule
docs.text:
PhysicsShape.capsule: (halfHeight: number, radius: number) -> PhysicsShape

A capsule along Y: a cylinder of halfHeight (without the caps) with a hemisphere of radius on each end.

docs.title: cylinder
docs.text:
PhysicsShape.cylinder: (halfHeight: number, radius: number) -> PhysicsShape

A cylinder along Y (wheels, barrels, posts).

docs.title: convex_hull
docs.text:
PhysicsShape.convex_hull: (points: { Vector3 }) -> PhysicsShape

The convex hull of these points (at least four, not in one plane).

docs.title: mesh
docs.text:
PhysicsShape.mesh: (vertices: { Vector3 }, indices: { number }) -> PhysicsShape

A static triangle mesh (terrain, buildings): indices are three per triangle. Meshes are only for static and kinematic bodies.

docs.title: height_field
docs.text:
PhysicsShape.height_field: (heights: { number }, size: number, offset: Vector3, scale: Vector3) -> PhysicsShape

A grid of heights (terrain): heights is size by size samples row by row (a power of two plus one works best, at least 2), at offset from the origin with the grid spaced by scale in x and z and heights multiplied by its y. A height of at least 1e30 is a hole.

docs.title: compound
docs.text:
PhysicsShape.compound: (children: { PhysicsShape }, positions: { Vector3 }, rotations: { Quat }) -> PhysicsShape

Several shapes at fixed places in one: the child i at positions[i] turned by rotations[i] (identity when the list is shorter).

docs.title: offset
docs.text:
PhysicsShape.offset: (shape: PhysicsShape, position: Vector3, rotation: Quat) -> PhysicsShape

The shape moved and turned inside its own space, which moves the body's origin relative to it (a box standing on the origin instead of centered on it).

docs.title: scaled
docs.text:
PhysicsShape.scaled: (shape: PhysicsShape, scale: Vector3) -> PhysicsShape

The shape stretched by scale; fails when the shape cannot be scaled so (IsValidScale).

docs.title: PhysicsWorld
docs.text:
Extends EngineObject.

The physics simulation of one ECS World: Jolt Physics with double-precision positions, stepped at a fixed rate. Entities get a Body with AddBody; a dynamic body's entity follows the simulation (its Transform is written, local to its parent, so the world's transform system then fills in the WorldTransform), and a kinematic body follows its entity.

docs.title: Properties
docs.text:
• step_seconds: number Seconds per step (PhysicsOptions.StepRate). Read-only.
  • steps: number The number of steps taken so far. Read-only.
  • body_count: number How many bodies the world has. Read-only.
  • dropped_events: number Events that did not fit the queue and were lost (see PhysicsOptions.EventCapacity). Read-only.
  • paused: boolean While true Update does nothing: no time is added and no step runs, so a pause menu stops the world and the bodies stay where they are.
  • interpolate: boolean Show bodies between their last two steps instead of at the last one: smooth at any frame rate, at the price of showing the past by up to a step.
  • gravity: Vector3
  • debug_draw: boolean Draw the bodies, joints and characters over the world (wireframes, colored by what each body is): the host that renders the world calls DrawDebug when this is on. Scripts turn it on with physics.debug_draw = true; the dev overlay has a checkbox.

docs.title: Signals
docs.text:
• stepping: Signal<number> Emitted before each fixed step with its length. Vehicle controllers and anything else that must act once per step belongs here, not in a frame callback.
  • contact_began: Signal<Entity, Entity, Vector3, Vector3> Two bodies started touching, at least one of them with BodyDesc.Events: the two entities, the contact point and the normal (pointing from the first to the second).
  • contact_ended: Signal<Entity, Entity>
  • sensor_entered: Signal<Entity, Entity> A body came into a sensor: the sensor's entity, then the other.
  • sensor_exited: Signal<Entity, Entity>
  • body_woke: Signal<Entity> A body with BodyDesc.Events woke up or went to sleep.
  • body_slept: Signal<Entity>

docs.title: has_body
docs.text:
function has_body(self, entity: Entity): boolean

Whether entity has a body here.

docs.title: add_body
docs.text:
function add_body(self, entity: Entity, desc: BodyDesc): ()

Gives entity a body made as desc describes, where its transform puts it now (its scale scales the shape). The entity gets a Transform if it has none.

docs.title: remove_body
docs.text:
function remove_body(self, entity: Entity): ()

Takes the body off entity (the entity stays, where the body left it).

docs.title: pose
docs.text:
function pose(self, entity: Entity): (Vector3, Quat)

The exact pose of the body in the world after the last step (the entity's own transform may show a blend between two steps, see Interpolate).

docs.title: teleport
docs.text:
function teleport(self, entity: Entity, position: Vector3, rotation: Quat): ()

Puts the body at this world pose at once, keeping its velocity, and its entity too (no blend). For a static body this is how it moves at all.

docs.title: add_force
docs.text:
function add_force(self, entity: Entity, force: Vector3): ()

A force in newtons through the center of mass, applied during the next step only (call it every step to push continuously).

docs.title: add_impulse
docs.text:
function add_impulse(self, entity: Entity, impulse: Vector3): ()

An instant change of momentum in newton seconds through the center of mass.

docs.title: update
docs.text:
function update(self, deltaSeconds: number): ()

Advances the simulation by deltaSeconds of game time in fixed steps (at most PhysicsOptions.MaxSubsteps a call; a slower frame loses time), then writes the bodies' poses to their entities. Call it once a frame, before World.Progress.

docs.title: create_character
docs.text:
function create_character(self, entity: Entity, height: number, radius: number, layers: number?, mask: number?): CharacterController

Makes a walking character for entity: a capsule of this height (feet to top, at least twice the radius) and radius, standing with its feet at the entity's position. layers and mask are the collision layers it is in and collides with.

docs.title: create_hitch
docs.text:
function create_hitch(self, hitchEntity: Entity, kind: HitchKind): Hitch

Makes a hitch of kind on hitchEntity, which must be under the entity of a dynamic body (the vehicle): its transform is the hitch's frame in the vehicle's space. Move the entity to lift what a mount hitch carries.

docs.title: create_vehicle
docs.text:
function create_vehicle(self, entity: Entity, desc: VehicleDesc): Vehicle

Makes a vehicle of desc on the dynamic body of entity. The vehicle's space is the entity's, +Z forward, +Y up, +X left. Set its inputs, drive_ratio and clutch in its stepping signal (or the world's); destroying the vehicle, its body or its entity ends it.

docs.title: get_mass
docs.text:
function get_mass(self, entity: Entity): number

The mass of the body of entity in kilograms (0 for a static or kinematic one).

docs.title: raycast
docs.text:
function raycast(self, origin: Vector3, direction: Vector3, maxDistance: number, mask: number?, ignore: Entity?): (boolean, Entity, Vector3, Vector3, number)

Casts a ray and returns the nearest hit: whether there was one, the entity, the hit point, the surface normal and the distance. mask picks the collision layers that count; ignore is an entity (the shooter's own body) the ray passes through. Sensors are never hit.

docs.title: cast_sphere
docs.text:
function cast_sphere(self, origin: Vector3, direction: Vector3, radius: number, maxDistance: number, mask: number?, ignore: Entity?): (boolean, Entity, Vector3, Vector3, number)

Sweeps a sphere along direction and returns the first body it touches: whether there was one, the entity, the point of contact, the normal and how far the sphere got.

docs.title: overlap_sphere
docs.text:
function overlap_sphere(self, center: Vector3, radius: number, mask: number?, ignore: Entity?): { Entity }

The entities of the bodies that touch this sphere (sensors excluded), each once.

docs.title: overlap_box
docs.text:
function overlap_box(self, center: Vector3, rotation: Quat, halfExtents: Vector3, mask: number?, ignore: Entity?): { Entity }

The entities of the bodies that touch this box (centered on center, turned by rotation), each once.

docs.title: create
docs.text:
PhysicsWorld.create: (ecs: World) -> PhysicsWorld

Makes the physics of an ECS world from a script (a game's own is the global physics). Destroy it, or let the script drop it, before the ECS world goes.

docs.title: SteamSystem
docs.text:
Extends EngineObject.

Objects of this class are refused to mods.

docs.title: Properties
docs.text:
• is_cloud_enabled: boolean Whether the cloud works: Steam is running, and the player has the cloud on for their account and for this game. Read-only.
  • is_active: boolean True when Steam started: the calls are real. False means every call does nothing. Read-only.
  • status: string What state Steam is in, in words a player can read: running, off, or why it did not start. Read-only.
  • restart_requested: boolean True when SteamOptions.AppId was set and the game was not started by Steam: Steam is starting it again, and this process should exit. Read-only.
  • user_id: string The player's SteamID64 as a decimal string, "" when Steam is not running. Read-only.
  • user_name: string The player's Steam name. Read-only.
  • app_id: number The game's Steam app id (0 when Steam is not running). Read-only.
  • build_id: number The build of the game Steam installed (changes with every upload to a branch). Read-only.
  • language: string The language the player chose for the game in Steam, as Steam names it (english, french, schinese…); "" when Steam is not running. Read-only.
  • ui_language: string The language of Steam's own interface. Read-only.
  • country: string The player's country (two letters), from their address. Read-only.
  • is_subscribed: boolean Whether the player owns the game (false for a family-shared or free-weekend copy that Steam still lets them play: IsSubscribed is about that account). Read-only.
  • is_steam_deck: boolean The game runs on a Steam Deck (Steam sets the SteamDeck environment variable there). Read-only.
  • is_big_picture: boolean Steam is in Big Picture mode (or the Deck's game mode). Read-only.
  • is_overlay_enabled: boolean Whether the overlay works in this run (Steam is running and the player did not switch it off). Read-only.

docs.title: Signals
docs.text:
• overlay_activated: Signal<boolean> The overlay opened (true) or closed: pause the game while it is open.
  • shutdown_requested: Signal<()> Steam wants the game to exit (the client is shutting down).
  • stats_received: Signal<boolean> The player's stats and achievements arrived from Steam (true) or could not be loaded.
  • stats_stored: Signal<boolean> A StoreStats finished.
  • achievement_stored: Signal<string, number, number> An achievement was unlocked or progressed, with its name and progress (0 and 0 for a plain unlock).
  • text_input_dismissed: Signal<boolean, string> Steam's on-screen keyboard closed, with whether the text was submitted and the text.
  • leaderboard_found: Signal<string, boolean> A leaderboard was looked up by name (true when it exists).
  • score_uploaded: Signal<string, boolean, number> A score was sent: the leaderboard, whether it worked, and the player's new global rank (0 when unchanged or failed).
  • scores_downloaded: Signal<string, { string }, { number }, { number }> Entries arrived: the leaderboard, then for each entry the player's id, global rank and score, in rank order.
  • workshop_item_installed: Signal<string> A Workshop item finished installing or updating on the disk (its id). Mods are read when the game starts: tell the player to restart for it to apply.
  • workshop_item_downloaded: Signal<string, boolean> A download that DownloadWorkshopItem started ended: the item id and whether it worked.
  • workshop_subscribed: Signal<string, boolean> A Subscribe finished: the item id and whether it worked.
  • workshop_unsubscribed: Signal<string, boolean> An Unsubscribe finished: the item id and whether it worked.

docs.title: cloud_quota
docs.text:
function cloud_quota(self): (number, number)

The cloud space of the game for this player, in bytes: the total, then what is left. 0 and 0 without Steam.

docs.title: update
docs.text:
function update(self): ()

Once a frame: runs Steam's callbacks and call results and emits their signals. Nothing else runs on another thread.

docs.title: owns_dlc
docs.text:
function owns_dlc(self, appId: number): boolean

The player owns the DLC appId.

docs.title: is_dlc_installed
docs.text:
function is_dlc_installed(self, appId: number): boolean

The DLC appId is owned and installed.

docs.title: activate_overlay
docs.text:
function activate_overlay(self, dialog: string?): ()

Opens a part of the overlay: friends, community, players, settings, officialgamegroup, stats or achievements; "" opens it as Shift+Tab does.

docs.title: open_web_page
docs.text:
function open_web_page(self, url: string): ()

Opens the overlay's browser on a web page.

docs.title: open_store
docs.text:
function open_store(self, appId: number): ()

Opens the store page of an app in the overlay (the game's own page, or a DLC's).

docs.title: set_rich_presence
docs.text:
function set_rich_presence(self, key: string, value: string): boolean

Sets a rich presence key, which friends see in their list (status is the line shown; others are for steam_display localization). An empty value removes the key.

docs.title: clear_rich_presence
docs.text:
function clear_rich_presence(self): ()

Removes all of this game's rich presence.

docs.title: trigger_screenshot
docs.text:
function trigger_screenshot(self): ()

Asks Steam to take a screenshot of the game's window (the player's screenshot key does it too).

docs.title: add_screenshot
docs.text:
function add_screenshot(self, path: string, width: number, height: number): boolean

Adds a screenshot file the game wrote (a JPEG, PNG or TGA on the disk) to the player's Steam library. False when Steam refused it.

docs.title: add_timeline_event
docs.text:
function add_timeline_event(self, title: string, description: string?, icon: string?, priority: number?, offsetSeconds: number?, featured: boolean?): ()

Marks a moment in the player's Steam timeline (the game recording): a title, a description, one of Steam's icon names (steam_achievement, steam_death, steam_marker…), a priority among the icons, and an offset in seconds from now (negative: something that just happened). A featured event is offered first as a clip.

docs.title: set_timeline_state
docs.text:
function set_timeline_state(self, description: string): ()

Sets the line of text that describes what the player is doing now on the timeline (a tooltip); "" clears it.

docs.title: set_timeline_mode
docs.text:
function set_timeline_mode(self, mode: string): ()

Tells the timeline what the game is doing: playing, staging (a lobby, a briefing), menus or loading; the recording skips menus and loading screens.

docs.title: show_text_input
docs.text:
function show_text_input(self, description: string, maxLength: number?, multiline: boolean?, password: boolean?): boolean

Opens Steam's on-screen keyboard (the overlay's, for a Deck or a controller) for a line of text; TextInputDismissed follows. False when it cannot be shown (the overlay is off).

docs.title: achievement
docs.text:
function achievement(self, name: string): boolean

Whether the achievement is unlocked (false when Steam is not running, or the name is not one of the game's).

docs.title: unlock_achievement
docs.text:
function unlock_achievement(self, name: string): boolean

Unlocks an achievement and sends it to Steam at once (it shows the pop-up). False when there is no such achievement or Steam is not running.

docs.title: clear_achievement
docs.text:
function clear_achievement(self, name: string): boolean

Locks an achievement again (for testing).

docs.title: achievement_progress
docs.text:

Shows a progress pop-up for an achievement that counts (current of max) without unlocking it; it also stores the progress.

docs.title: achievement_names
docs.text:
function achievement_names(self): { string }

The names of the game's achievements, as set up in Steamworks.

docs.title: stat_int
docs.text:

The value of an integer stat (0 when there is none).

docs.title: stat_float
docs.text:

The value of a float stat (0 when there is none).

docs.title: set_stat_int

Sets an integer stat in memory; StoreStats sends the changes.

docs.title: set_stat_float
docs.text:

Sets a float stat in memory; StoreStats sends the changes.

docs.title: store_stats
docs.text:
function store_stats(self): boolean

Sends the changed stats and achievements to Steam; StatsStored says when it is done. Do not call it more than once a few minutes: Steam limits it.

docs.title: reset_all_stats
docs.text:
function reset_all_stats(self, achievements: boolean): boolean

Resets every stat, and the achievements too when asked. For testing a new player.

docs.title: find_leaderboard
docs.text:
function find_leaderboard(self, name: string): ()

Looks a leaderboard up by name; LeaderboardFound follows. The other leaderboard calls do this by themselves when they need to.

docs.title: upload_score
docs.text:
function upload_score(self, leaderboard: string, score: number, keepBest: boolean?): ()

Sends a score; ScoreUploaded follows. With keepBest the leaderboard keeps the player's better score (by the leaderboard's sort order), otherwise this one replaces it.

docs.title: download_scores
docs.text:
function download_scores(self, leaderboard: string, from: number?, to: number?, kind: string?): ()

Asks for the entries from rank from to to (1 is the best) of kind (global, around_user, where the range is relative to the player, or friends); ScoresDownloaded follows, with no entries when it failed.

docs.title: subscribed_items
docs.text:
function subscribed_items(self): { string }

The ids of the Workshop items the player is subscribed to.

docs.title: subscribe
docs.text:
function subscribe(self, itemId: string): ()

Subscribes to a Workshop item (Steam downloads it); WorkshopSubscribed follows.

docs.title: unsubscribe
docs.text:

Unsubscribes from a Workshop item (Steam deletes it); WorkshopUnsubscribed follows.

docs.title: download_workshop_item
docs.text:
function download_workshop_item(self, itemId: string): boolean

Asks Steam to download (or update) an item now, ahead of the others; WorkshopItemDownloaded follows. False when Steam refused.

docs.title: workshop_item_folder
docs.text:
function workshop_item_folder(self, itemId: string): string

The folder an installed item is in, or "" when it is not installed (yet).

docs.title: create_inactive
docs.text:
SteamSystem.create_inactive: () -> SteamSystem

Makes an inactive Steam system from a script, which touches nothing of Steam: for testing the game's own code that expects a steam global. A game's real one is the global steam.

Whether Steam's library can be loaded.

docs.title: UiDataModel
docs.text:
Extends EngineObject.

A data model: a script's table tied to documents.

{{score}}

shows score of the table; data-if, data-for, data-class-, data-style- and data-value (which writes back what the player types) use it too, and data-event-click="buy(1)" calls the table's function buy. The table is read when RmlUi needs a value: change it and say so with Dirty (or change a top-level field with Set), and the elements that show it are updated at the next frame.

docs.title: Properties
docs.text:
• name: string The name documents use in data-model. Read-only.
  • is_open: boolean Whether the model still exists (it is closed with Close, when the module that opened it reloads, and when the UI ends). Read-only.

docs.title: dirty
docs.text:
function dirty(self, name: string?): ()

Says that the field (a top-level one) or, with no name, everything changed: the elements that show it are updated at the next frame. A change inside a list or struct needs the name of the whole.

docs.title: set
docs.text:
function set(self, name: string, value: any): boolean

Sets a top-level field of the table and marks it dirty.

docs.title: is_dirty
docs.text:
function is_dirty(self, name: string): boolean

Whether the field changed since the last frame updated the documents.

docs.text:

Removes the model. Close the documents that use it first.

docs.title: UiElement
docs.text:
Extends EngineObject.

An element of a document (a div, a text node, a whole document) as scripts hold it. The object is a handle: it names the element without keeping it alive, so one whose element has been destroyed (its document was closed, an ancestor was destroyed) is IsAlive false and every call on it does nothing or answers "none". An element made with CreateElement or CreateText belongs to the object that holds it until it is put in a tree with Append or InsertBefore; an element nobody ever put in a tree is destroyed when the script lets go of it, and one in a tree lives as long as the tree does. Elements are made, moved and changed here.

docs.title: Properties
docs.text:
• is_alive: boolean Whether the element still exists. Read-only.
  • tag: string The tag (div, body), or empty for a dead element. Read-only.
  • id: string The element's id (the id attribute; ids are unique in a document).
  • class_name: string The classes, separated by spaces: what the style rules (.card) match.
  • inner_rml: string The RML of what is inside the element; setting it replaces the children.
  • text: string The text of a text node (made with CreateText); empty for any other element.
  • is_visible: boolean Whether it can be seen: not display: none or visibility: hidden, itself or any element above it. Read-only.
  • parent: UiElement? The element it is in, or nothing for a document or an element in no tree. Read-only.
  • child_count: number The number of elements and text nodes directly inside. Read-only.
  • document: UiElement? The document the element is in (a document is its own). Read-only.

docs.title: show
docs.text:
function show(self): ()

Makes the document visible (and it starts to be drawn and to take input).

docs.title: close
docs.text:
function close(self): ()

Unloads the document: everything in it is destroyed. Call it on the document.

docs.title: add_style
docs.text:
function add_style(self, rcss: string): boolean

Adds style rules (RCSS) to the document this element is in, on top of its own.

docs.title: create_element
docs.text:
function create_element(self, tag: string): UiElement?

A new element with the tag (div, span, input...) in this element's document, in no tree yet.

docs.title: create_text
docs.text:

Calls handler with a UiEvent whenever an event of this type (click, mousedown, keydown, change, focus...) reaches the element on its way up from what was hit, or, with capture, on its way down. Returns a number for UiSystem.Unlisten. The listener goes when the element does.

An event that reached a listener (UiElement.Listen). It is only good inside the handler: afterwards its calls do nothing.

docs.title: Vehicle
docs.text:
Extends EngineObject.

A vehicle on a dynamic body: wheels with suspension and tires, or tracks, an engine and a clutch (Jolt's VehicleConstraint). The game owns the gearbox: it sets DriveRatio (the signed overall ratio it wants, 0 for neutral) and Clutch in the Stepping signal, which runs before each physics step, together with the driver's inputs, and the vehicle gives them to Jolt. Make one with PhysicsWorld.CreateVehicle.

docs.title: Properties
docs.text:
• entity: Entity The entity of the vehicle's body. Read-only.
  • forward: number Throttle: -1 to 1 (negative backs up in a gearbox that reverses by throttle; the usual gearbox uses DriveRatio's sign).
  • steering: number -1 to 1: positive turns toward +X (the vehicle's left, in its +Z-forward space), negative toward -X.
  • brake: number
  • handbrake: number
  • drive_ratio: number The overall ratio between engine and wheels the game drives through, signed: negative reverses; 0 is neutral. Set it in Stepping.
  • clutch: number How far the clutch is engaged: 0 drives nothing, 1 is fully engaged. Set it in Stepping.
  • is_ready: boolean Whether the vehicle is working (its body exists and the wheels were built). Read-only.
  • gear_ratio: number The gear ratio the transmission is in now. Read-only.
  • engine_rpm: number Read-only.
  • engine_torque: number The torque the engine gives at the throttle that reached it, in N·m. Read-only.
  • engine_load: number The throttle that reached the engine, 0 to 1. Read-only.
  • engine_peak_power_rpm: number The rpm where the engine's power (torque times rpm) peaks, from its curve. Read-only.
  • brake_capacity: number What all the brakes give together, in N·m. Read-only.
  • speed_kmh: number How fast it moves along its forward axis, in km/h (negative backing up). Read-only.
  • wheel_count: number How many wheels it has. Read-only.

docs.title: Signals
docs.text: • stepping: Signal<number> Emitted before each fixed step with its length, before the inputs reach Jolt: the game's driving logic (its gearbox, assists, ABS) belongs here.

docs.title: get_wheel_compression
docs.text:
function get_wheel_compression(self, index: number): number

How far the suspension is compressed, 0 (extended) to 1.

docs.title: get_wheel_steer_degrees
docs.text:
function get_wheel_steer_degrees(self, index: number): number

How far the wheel is turned about its steering axis, in degrees (positive toward +X, like Steering).

docs.title: get_wheel_rpm
docs.text:
function get_wheel_rpm(self, index: number): number

The wheel's rotation speed in revolutions per minute.

docs.title: get_wheel_contact_point
docs.text:
function get_wheel_contact_point(self, index: number): Vector3

The point where the wheel touches the ground (the world's origin if it does not).

docs.title: get_wheel_contact_entity
docs.text:
function get_wheel_contact_entity(self, index: number): Entity

The entity of the body the wheel stands on, or 0.

docs.title: get_wheel_readings
docs.text:
function get_wheel_readings(self): { number }

Four numbers for each wheel, the ones the driving assists need: 1 if it touches the ground (else 0), its angular velocity in rad/s, the load it carries in newtons (its suspension's force) and the grip of its tire (0 for a track's wheel).

docs.title: set_brake_factor
docs.text:
function set_brake_factor(self, index: number, factor: number): ()

Scales one wheel's brake torque for the next steps: 0 releases it, 1 is full. An ABS sets it every step.

docs.title: VehicleDesc
docs.text:
Extends EngineObject.

A vehicle: its engine, drivetrain and wheels. Give it to PhysicsWorld.CreateVehicle with the entity of a dynamic body.

Create one with VehicleDesc.new().

docs.title: Properties
docs.text:
• drive: DriveKind
  • wheels: { WheelDesc }
  • engine_max_torque: number Torque at the best rev, in N·m.
  • engine_min_rpm: number
  • engine_max_rpm: number
  • engine_torque_curve: { number } The torque at each rev as a share of the maximum, sampled evenly from 0 to the maximum rpm (at least two values); empty is the same torque at every rev.
  • engine_inertia: number The engine's flywheel inertia in kg·m².
  • differential_ratio: number The final drive: engine revs per wheel rev, before the gear the game drives through.
  • clutch_slip_rpm: number How many rpm the clutch slips at full engine torque: lower is a stiffer clutch.
  • track_brake_torque: number Brake torque of a track's sprocket (tracked vehicles).
  • max_pitch_roll_angle: number The vehicle's body is helped upright beyond this pitch or roll, in degrees.

docs.title: WheelDesc
docs.text:
Extends EngineObject.

One wheel of a vehicle. The vehicle's space has +Z forward, +Y up and +X to its left (glTF's). Its Position is where the wheel's center sits with its suspension fully extended: the suspension reaches SuspensionLength above that, and the wheel rests somewhere in that travel under the load.

Create one with WheelDesc.new().

docs.title: Properties
docs.text:
• position: Vector3 Where the wheel's center is with the suspension extended, in the vehicle's space.
  • entity: Entity An entity (usually a child of the vehicle's entity) whose local transform follows the wheel each frame: its place on the suspension, steered and spinning. 0 for none.
  • radius: number
  • width: number
  • suspension_length: number How far the wheel can move up from its extended position.
  • suspension_frequency: number The suspension's natural frequency in Hz: higher is stiffer.
  • suspension_damping: number 1 is critically damped.
  • max_steer_angle: number How far the wheel turns at full steering, in degrees (0: it does not steer).
  • steer_ratio: number How much of the steering a wheel takes, and which way: 1 for front wheels, -1 for rear steering, 1 on every axle for crab steering. A wheel with no steer angle counts as ratio 0, the fixed axle. With two wheels of different ratios the steered wheels turn about one turning center (Ackermann).
  • powered: boolean Whether the engine drives it (wheeled vehicles) or it is the track's sprocket (tracked).
  • max_brake_torque: number Brake torque in N·m at full brake.
  • max_handbrake_torque: number
  • friction: number Scales the tire's grip (1 is Jolt's default tire).
  • torque_share: number The share of the engine's torque this wheel's axle gets, among the powered axles. By the load on the axles, a lightly loaded front axle would spin.
  • brake_factor: number Scales the brake torque while driving: an ABS or a one-sided brake sets it per step (see Vehicle.SetBrakeFactor).

docs.title: Properties
docs.text:
• delta_time: number The time step of the current Progress; what systems read for their delta time. Read-only.
  • frame: number The number of frames Progress has run. Read-only.

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text:
Apogee is maintained by one person for now: reviews take time, and scope is guarded. The rules are in CONTRIBUTING.md; in short:

  • Open an issue or a discussion before a big change. Bugs need a minimal reproduction.
  • Pull requests that drift from the engine's purpose (see the Introduction) are declined.
  • Conventional Commits, and every commit signed off (git commit -s, the DCO).
  • Every feature has tests and a Manual page. Warnings are errors; no runtime reflection in Source/.
  • AI assistance is fine; submitting code you do not understand is not.

Pages for contributors: Help wanted (what we need and how to check your work), Continuous integration and Writing docs.

docs.title: Continuous integration
docs.text:
GitHub Actions builds, tests and publishes every push to main and every pull request. The layout follows the habit of large open-source engines: runner.yml is the entry point and calls one workflow per concern, and each of those can also be started by hand from the Actions tab.

Workflow What it does runner.yml the entry point: static checks first, then the three platforms and the docs in parallel static_checks.yml the DCO sign-off of every commit of a pull request, no CRLF or trailing whitespace, Git LFS pointers (git lfs fsck --pointers), and actionlint on the workflows linux_builds.yml Tests: Release build and every test project, GPU tests on lavapipe (Mesa's software Vulkan) with the validation layer, the bindings generator's tests with libclang. NativeAOT: ./build.sh aot, the Luau tests and a fixture game from the published binary, rendered offscreen, shipped as a pack and without the shader compiler windows_builds.yml Tests: Release build and every test project. NativeAOT: the publish, the Luau tests and the fixture game, with no GPU macos_builds.yml Apple silicon and Intel: Release build, the tests (the Metal GPU tests skip unless the runner's GPU qualifies), the NativeAOT publish and the fixture game, uploaded as artifacts. The Intel job is experimental while a rare crash is investigated (see Help wanted) docs.yml ./build.sh docs (the API reference, then mkdocs build --strict); on a push to main, publishes the site to the apogeeengine/docs repository's GitHub Pages thirdparty_*.yml manual workflows that build the vendored binaries we cannot take from upstream (GameNetworkingSockets, OpenAL Soft, SDL for Linux). Their recipes and the checksums are in ThirdParty/README.md

.github/actions/setup is the part the build workflows share: the Git LFS objects of the platform (cached by object id, so a push does not spend the repository's LFS bandwidth), the .NET SDK and the native libraries (Flecs, Luau, and so on).

docs.title: Rules the workflows hold to
docs.text:
• Tests are not samples. CI runs Tests/ and the fixture game in Tests/Fixtures; nothing runs Samples/, no test depends on one, and there are no reference screenshots of samples.
  • Required natives fail, they do not skip. APOGEE_REQUIRE_NATIVE lists the native libraries that must load on each platform; APOGEE_REQUIRE_VULKAN, APOGEE_REQUIRE_CLANG and APOGEE_REQUIRE_METAL_COMPILER do the same for the GPU, libclang and Apple's shader compiler.
  • Run what CI runs. ./build.sh test is dotnet test, and ./build.sh aot is the publish step: the same commands a developer uses.

docs.title: Reproducing a failure
docs.text: Linux needs mesa-vulkan-drivers and vulkan-validationlayers for the GPU tests (lavapipe is the software device). Windows and macOS runners have no usable Vulkan or Metal device: a GPU test that skips there ran on Linux.

docs.title: Help wanted
docs.text: The engine is developed on Linux with Vulkan, and checked on Windows and macOS by CI. That leaves work that needs hardware, platforms or a second pair of eyes the maintainer does not have. Each task below says what exists, what is missing and how to check your work. Open an issue or a discussion before starting a big one, and read CONTRIBUTING.md.

docs.title: Metal backend
docs.text:
What exists. Everything compiles, and CI checks what a GPU-less runner can: the Objective-C shim Native/metal_c builds, its bindings (Apogee.Native.Metal) resolve, the engine's Metal shading language is accepted by Apple's own compiler, and the backend Apogee.Graphics.Metal (device, buffers, textures, argument-buffer bindless heap, pipelines, command encoders, CAMetalLayer swapchain, frame loop) is complete on paper. GitHub's macOS runners have a paravirtual GPU that is not Metal 3, so none of the Metal GPU tests has ever run: expect bugs.

Needs: a Mac with macOS 15 or later and a Metal 3 GPU with tier 2 argument buffers (Apple silicon, or an Intel Mac from 2017 on). Either architecture helps, because a bug can be in one only.

Task Where to look Done when Run it and fix what breaks. Start with --gpu-info, then APOGEE_REQUIRE_METAL=1 ./build.sh test, then the viewer and the samples. Metal on a Mac, Source/Apogee.Graphics/Metal/, Native/metal_c/ the GPU tests pass with no skips, and the viewer draws the courtyard in a window Measure the image tolerance. Metal's rasterizer is not Mesa's, which made the reference images; the Metal bound (mean 2, worst channel 64) is a guess. GpuTest.ReferenceTolerance in Tests/Apogee.Graphics.Tests/GpuFixture.cs the bound is tightened to what Macs measure, or Metal gets reference images of its own GPU timings. FrameLoop.Timings is empty on Metal. Counter sample buffers (MTLCounterSampleBuffer) sample at encoder boundaries, and not on every GPU. MetalFrameLoop, MetalDevice.SupportsTimestamps, apogee_metal.h GpuScopesAreTimedAndLabelled runs (is not skipped) and passes on Metal Shader library cache. Metal shading language is compiled with newLibraryWithSource every start; an MTLBinaryArchive would keep the result. MetalDevice.CreateComputePipeline and CreateGraphicsPipeline the second start does not compile A CI runner with a real Metal GPU. A self-hosted Mac makes APOGEE_REQUIRE_METAL=1 possible: point macos_builds.yml at it (the probe step already turns the requirement on when a GPU qualifies). .github/workflows/macos_builds.yml, "GPUs (Metal probe)" the Metal tests are required in CI Check the Intel (osx-x64) NativeAOT build. CI publishes it as an artifact, but it has only been built. the apogee-osx-x64 artifact the fixture game, a sample and the Luau tests run from it

docs.title: Windows testing
docs.text:
What exists. CI builds and tests Release on windows-latest (a software GPU at best), and the NativeAOT runtime runs the fixture game headless. Nobody has run the editor, the samples or the GPU tests on real Windows hardware.

Needs: a Windows 10 or 11 machine with a Vulkan 1.3 GPU (AMD, NVIDIA or Intel; Windows on Arm too).

Task Done when Run it. ./build.sh test, then the viewer sample and the editor (dotnet run --project Source/Apogee.Editor -- Samples/Mods/game). Report what fails, with --gpu-info's output. an issue per problem, or a "works" note in the Windows discussion with your GPU and driver Controllers, high-DPI, multi-monitor, fullscreen. The input and window code is checked on Linux only. what breaks is reported or fixed NativeAOT on Windows. ./build.sh aot and the games' commands in Building. the fixture game and the Luau tests run from the published binary

docs.title: Reviewing
docs.text: The maintainer works alone, so every kind of review helps: the unsafe and interop code (Apogee.Interop, the generated bindings' layout checks, the native shims in Native/), the public APIs (naming, ownership, what throws), the shaders, and the Manual (a page that does not match the code is a bug). Open an issue with what you found, or a pull request.

docs.title: Expanding the engine
docs.text: Features that fit the scope in CONTRIBUTING.md are welcome: rendering features (shadows, post-processing, terrain), editor panels, tools, samples, the editor (importing models and assets, materials, animations, exporting a game: it is very bare-bones), more Luau API, performance work with a benchmark in Samples/Benchmarks. Every feature comes with tests and a Manual page. Ask first if it is big.

docs.title: Tell us if you hit this
docs.text: The Apogee.Ecs.Tests test program crashed twice on the Intel macOS CI runner (that job is experimental, so a failure does not fail the run) with a floating-point exception (SIGFPE) in a non-main thread, and passed on other runs. It has not been explained. The CI prints the crash report's faulting thread when it happens again.

docs.title: Writing docs
docs.text:
The documentation is Markdown in Docs/, built with MkDocs and the Material theme, and published at apogeeengine.github.io/docs. It lives next to the code so that a pull request changes both.

Docs/
  about/            introduction, FAQ, license
  getting-started/  building, samples
  manual/           one folder per area: core, native, platform, graphics, physics, audio, network, scripting, content, ui, tools
  api/              the generated reference (not committed, see below), with a committed index page each
  contributing/     for people who work on the engine

docs.title: Building the site
docs.text:
pip install mkdocs-material
./build.sh docs          # the API reference, then the site into Bin/site (mkdocs --strict: a broken link fails the build)
./build.sh docs serve    # the same, then a local server that reloads when a page changes

./build.sh docs first writes the API reference, which is why you do not run mkdocs directly:

  • C#: DocFX (a pinned local dotnet tool, .config/dotnet-tools.json) reads the XML documentation comments of the libraries listed in Tools/docfx/docfx.json and writes one page per type into Docs/api/csharp. The raw bindings (Apogee.Native.*) are left out. Document public members with /// comments: that is the C# reference.
  • Luau: Apogee.Runtime --luau-docs Docs/api/luau writes one page per class and library from the registry. The text comes from the same /// comments of [ApogeeClass], [Property], [Method] and [Signal] members, so documenting them documents the script API too.

Both folders are git-ignored apart from their index.md.

docs.title: Style
docs.text:
• A page explains how a feature fits together and why; the API reference lists the members. Show the smallest example that runs.
  • Say what is missing and what is untested. A page that does not match the code is a bug.
  • Relative links between pages (../core/ecs.md), so the strict build checks them.
  • No screenshots of samples as references: samples are run by hand.

docs.title: Building
docs.text:
Requires the .NET 10 SDK, CMake and Ninja (native libraries), Git LFS (prebuilt binaries are LFS objects: run git lfs install once before cloning) and clang (only to regenerate bindings).

./build.sh                       # dotnet build Apogee.slnx
./build.sh test                  # dotnet test
./build.sh native                # the shared libraries in Native/ (Flecs, Luau, cimgui) into Bin/native/<rid>
./build.sh aot                   # NativeAOT publish of Apogee.Runtime and Samples/Viewer into Bin/publish, then their shaders compiled ahead of time
./build.sh docs                  # this Manual and the API reference, built with mkdocs --strict into Bin/site (see Writing docs)
./build.sh bindings [lib…]       # regenerate Source/Apogee.Native.*/Generated

build.ps1 is the same on Windows. A .env file (gitignored) is loaded by both wrappers.

docs.title: Native libraries
docs.text:
Libraries that are vendored as binaries live in ThirdParty/<lib>/lib/<rid>; libraries built from source are built by ./build.sh native into Bin/native/<rid>. Either way ThirdParty/NativeLibraries.props copies the ones for the current platform next to a project's output, where NativeLibraries finds them (see Interop). ThirdParty/README.md says where each library comes from and how it was built.

Steamworks is proprietary. Valve lets us publish the SDK's redistributable_bin libraries, which are in the repository; ./build.sh sdk steam <zip> refreshes them from a newer SDK and unpacks the headers (git-ignored) that regenerating the bindings needs. Which files are unpacked, and why, is in ThirdParty/README.md.

Shared libraries on Linux are linked with --no-undefined: a missing source file fails the build instead of the first call.

docs.title: Warnings
docs.text: Warnings are errors, including the trimming and NativeAOT analyzers, for everything under Source/.

docs.title: Continuous integration
docs.text: Every push to main and every pull request builds, tests and publishes on Linux, Windows and macOS: see Continuous integration.

docs.title: Mods sample
docs.text:
Samples/Mods is a small game made only of packages, with mods that change its data and run scripts, shown by two panels. It is also what CI runs end to end: the package loader, definitions with schemas and patches, the sandbox, packs, and a rendered image.

Apogee.Runtime --game Samples/Mods/game --user /tmp/mods-user              # a window with the panels
Apogee.Runtime --game Samples/Mods/game --user /tmp/mods-user --watch      # and edit while it runs (see Hot reload)

game/ is the game's folder (res://): packages/base_game is its one base package, and dev_mods/ holds the mods of a development build (a player's mods go in user://mods, the same layout). --user is where user:// is; mods may write only user://moddata/<their id>/.

Package Shows base_game a schema for Crate (an enumeration, a default, a repeated Tag, a map of prices), two crates, a module (lib/util.luau) and a script with the two panels bigger_crates a dependency on base_game (^1.0) and gameVersion; a patch of the wooden crate (weight, size, and <Tag append="true">) and a new crate (gold); require("@base_game/lib/util"); writing its own data folder broken_mod a script with a bug: the error is logged with its file and line, the package is marked failed, and the game goes on needs_ghost a dependency on a mod that is not there: it does not load, and packages.list() says why

The Packages panel is packages.list(): which packages loaded, in load order, and for those that did not, why. The Crates panel is defs.all("Crate") after every package's content was merged: the wooden crate is 20 kg and large with three tags (the base game's two and the mod's), and the gold crate is the mod's. Delete bigger_crates and run again, and the panel shows the base game's numbers: nothing else changes.

docs.title: Things to try
docs.text:
• --watch, then change weight in dev_mods/bigger_crates/data/crates.xml, or a line in lib/util.luau: the panel changes without a restart.
  • Misspell an attribute in crates.xml: the schema reports it (defs.problems(), and the log) with the file and line, and the crate is still there.
  • Make needs_ghost load by adding a ghost_mod package next to it; make bigger_crates stop loading with <Dependency id="base_game" version=">=2.0"/>.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
• Samples/Mods/tests/util.test.luau: the module's functions, with --luau-test (run by hand).
  • Nothing in CI runs this sample. What it shows is tested on a fixture game of its own: Tests/Fixtures/ShippedGame (a package, a mod, a UI document with a script and a data model, and an ImGui panel) runs headless, from a pack and rendered on lavapipe in CI, and Tests/Apogee.Runtime.Tests and Tests/Apogee.Mods.Tests cover the loading, patching, dependency and failure rules.

docs.title: Scripting sample
docs.text:
Samples/Scripting is a program in Luau only: boxes that move and bounce in a cube, a panel with their count and a speed slider, and tests. It uses the scripting layer, and shows how a game's scripts are laid out.

  • sim.luau is a module. sim.install(world, settings) defines the components (Position, Velocity, the Box tag) and two systems: Move carries every box by its velocity times settings.speed and the frame's time step, and Bounce runs after it ("post_update") and puts a box that left the cube back on the wall, turned around. sim.spawn makes boxes from a small deterministic generator, so a run is the same every time. The settings table is read by the systems each frame: the panel's slider changes it.
  • main.luau is the program. The host gives it world; it installs the simulation, spawns 50 boxes, and registers a gui function with devtools.on_gui that draws the panel (imgui.begin_window, imgui.slider_float, imgui.button) and devtools.watches the speed and the frame in the debug window.
  • tests/sim.test.luau runs sim in a world of its own for as many frames as each case needs: spawning, the same places every run, motion by velocity, the speed setting, a bounce at the wall, and sixty boxes staying inside the cube for ten seconds.
Apogee.Runtime --luau-test Samples/Scripting
Apogee.Runtime --run Samples/Scripting/main.luau                    # in a window, with the panel and the dev overlay
Apogee.Runtime --run Samples/Scripting/main.luau --frames 120 --headless

This is a sample: you run it by hand, and nothing in CI runs it (the Luau library it uses is tested by Tests/Luau and the engine's own test projects). For luau-lsp, Apogee.Runtime --luau-defs Bin/defs writes the definitions and the sample's .luaurc points the engine alias at them. See Scripting, Runtime and Luau tests and Dev tools.

docs.title: UI sample
docs.text:
Samples/UI is a small game whose UI is plain RmlUi: a main menu, an options screen, a pause menu, and a HUD over a physics scene, written as RML and RCSS documents with Luau scripts and data models, plus a mod that adds a panel to the HUD. It is the model for how a game and its mods build UI with the ui surface: documents that carry their own scripts and data models.

Apogee.Runtime --game Samples/UI/game --user /tmp/ui-user          # Start, play; Esc pauses and resumes
echo playing > /tmp/ui-user/autostart.txt                          # menu, options, playing or paused: where the game starts
Apogee.Runtime --luau-test Samples/UI                              # the sample's own tests

A window, a keyboard and a mouse are all it needs. Like the other samples it is run by hand (and with --watch to edit while it runs), and nothing in CI runs it: the engine's behavior it relies on is tested in the engine's own tests.

docs.title: The game
docs.text:
game/packages/base_ui is the base package. Its files are small, and each has one job:

File What it holds main.luau Ties the scene to the screen (the world is paused except while playing; Start builds the scene and launches the ball), and starts the screens. lib/state.luau The game's state as plain values (screen, volume, theme, the speeds), the flow between screens (start, open_options, close_options, to_menu, escape) and the formatting helpers. It tells whoever registered (on_screen, on_theme) when something changed. Nothing else knows what a screen is called, and nothing here knows what a document is. lib/screens.luau Loads the four documents once, shows and hides them as the screen changes (the pause menu is shown after the HUD, so it is drawn over it), puts the theme class on their bodies, and sends Escape to state.escape. lib/hud.luau The hud data model ({{speed}}, {{top_speed}}, {{fps}}, the minimap dot) and the slots: hud.add_panel("hud_right", rml, rcss) puts a panel in a place the HUD document reserves. lib/options.luau The options data model (the theme's name, the volume as text and as a bar width) and what the buttons do to it. lib/scene.luau The scene behind the UI: a ground, a pyramid of crates and a ball (physics bodies, drawn as debug wireframes: the sample ships no models), a camera entity, and a system that reads the ball into the HUD's model every frame. ui/theme.rcss The look: colors are custom properties on body (--surface, --fg, --primary...), and body.light redefines them, so putting the class light on a document's body switches the theme. Cards, buttons, rows and the volume bar are rules here. ui/*.rml, ui/*.luau A document and its script for the menu, the options, the pause menu; the HUD has no script, only its data model. A script is a <script src> of the document, and its functions are what the onclick="on_start()" attributes call.
